compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The Gerrit Verified gate executes workflow files from TRUSTED MAIN, not the patchset (proven
on change 2115 PS1: its own run 32587991195 still executed main's stale `--timeout=20`,
headSha 6a5c88027c5). pytest-timeout precedence is marker > CLI > `PYTEST_TIMEOUT` env > ini
(`get_env_settings` / `_get_item_settings` in `pytest_timeout.py`), so the
`--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` CLI flags on `_build-and-test.yml`'s two shared-tier
lanes (the default-suite and integration `run:` commands) permanently shadow any future
per-test-budget change carried in `pyproject.toml`: a budget fix can never be exercised by its
own Verified run — the class of failure that made 2115 PS1 fail its own gate. Bug
`3fa7-94ba-42aa-4623` was ultimately landed by an operator-cast Verified+1, which is not a
repeatable path.

## Approach

Single-source the shared-tier budget: REMOVE the `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` CLI
flags from both `_build-and-test.yml` lanes and let `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` (`timeout =
300`, `timeout_method = "thread"`, at `pyproject.toml:662-663`) govern. This is the
ecosystem-standard shape — scikit-learn, pandas and numpy pass no `--timeout` on their CI
pytest command lines; the budget lives in config. With the flags gone, a patchset that changes
the ini budget IS exercised by its own Verified run, because the ini travels with the patchset
while workflow files come from trusted main.

Effective budgets do not change: the lanes ran at CLI `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`
and the ini already carries the identical values, so removal only moves authority (the
before/after is documented in the commit message). The eleven other `--timeout=` lanes
(external-integration, optionality, eval-discipline, test.yml, structured-output-baseline)
keep their own larger calibrated CLI budgets — they drive live services, clean-venv installs
and eval sweeps, and several run outside this repo's rootdir where the ini is not in play.

The previously drafted conftest-floor mechanism (branch `preserve/timeout-floor-hardening`,
commit `b38bf9a4748`) is rejected and does not land: pytest-timeout resolves
`config._env_timeout` at session start read-only, so a conftest floor has no supported hook
point and no OSS precedent. That branch is mined for its reusable test assets only (the
parity-contract rewrites and the lane-flag removals); its `tests/_timeout_floor.py`, conftest
hook, and docs floor section are discarded, and the branch (local-only; it has no `origin`
ref) is deleted after mining.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — remove `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`
  from the default-suite and integration `run:` commands; rewrite the adjacent hang-guard
  comments to say the budget lives in the ini and these lanes are deliberately flag-free.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — rewrite
  `test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget` to assert the two shared-tier
  lanes carry NO `--timeout`/`--timeout-method` flags (and that the ini budget is present and
  positive, since it becomes their only guard); update
  `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` so a lane may satisfy the guard by
  inheriting the asserted-real ini keys (budget positive, `thread` method) instead of an
  explicit flag, while a lane that DOES set a flag must still use the `thread` method.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — update the sentence stating the two lanes are "held equal to the
  ini value" to say they are held flag-free (single-sourced from the ini).

## Testing

RED-first: the rewritten parity contract asserting no `--timeout`/`--timeout-method` on the
shared-tier lanes is the oracle — it fails against the current workflow (flags present) and
passes after the removal. The hang-guard sweep keeps its negative power: it still requires
every other pytest lane to carry an explicit budget flag with the `thread` method, and the ini
fallback it now accepts for flag-free lanes is asserted real (`timeout` positive,
`timeout_method = "thread"`) rather than assumed. An unmarked hung test remains bounded: the
out-of-process negative arms in `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` prove the ini keys alone
expire a hung body, setup, and teardown. `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the targeted
suites (`pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py`) run
green before push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Neither `_build-and-test.yml` shared-tier lane passes `--timeout` or `--timeout-method`
      on its pytest command line; checked by the rewritten parity contract failing if a flag
      reappears.
- [x] The ini remains the lanes' real guard: the parity contracts assert
      `[tool.pytest.ini_options].timeout` is present and positive and `timeout_method` is
      `thread`, and the existing out-of-process negative arms in `test_timeout_budget.py`
      prove those keys alone expire a hung test (no weakening of the hang guard).
- [x] The hang-guard sweep still requires an explicit `--timeout` flag (with
      `--timeout-method=thread`) on every pytest lane outside `_build-and-test.yml`; checked
      by `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` passing over the unchanged
      eleven calibrated lanes.
- [x] The effective shared-tier budget is unchanged (300 s, thread method, before and after);
      documented in the commit message and checked by the ini config arm in
      `test_timeout_budget.py` still pinning `timeout = 300`.
- [x] Branch `preserve/timeout-floor-hardening` is deleted after mining (local `git branch -D`;
      it has no `origin` ref, verified via `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/preserve/*'`);
      recorded in this ticket's close evidence.
